semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL clause requires the door-closing alternatives to resolve deterministically between DoorShutWithItem and ReadytoCook depending on whether cooking time is zero or set. The exact closed-model facts show transition:line:23 (DoorOpenWithItem -Door_Closed_with_0_time-> DoorShutWithItem) and transition:line:24 (DoorOpenWithItem -Time_Set-> ReadytoCook) both have guard=null per inspection_equivalent_facts, so the time-zero-vs-set distinction is encoded only as two differently named trigger events rather than as an evaluated guard condition, which is exactly what the candidate observes. The strongest alternative reading is that distinct event names alone make the alternatives trivially non-colliding at the event level, obviating any guard-level disjointness concern. However, this alternative cannot be marked as a surviving defeater here because the supplied defeater_evidence_reference_catalog for this obligation is empty: there is no exact catalog token establishing that event-level distinctness is an accepted substitute for the NL's implied evaluated-condition disjointness, nor any exact fact showing the two events are themselves guaranteed mutually exclusive at runtime. Absent such supplied evidence, the event-naming alternative does not rise above a conceivable reading and is treated as defeated; the guard=null facts on both transitions establish the candidate's obligation as an exact, currently-unaddressed semantic gap rather than an unresolved ambiguity.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The two alternatives are triggered by textually distinct events (Door_Closed_with_0_time vs Time_Set) rather than one shared event distinguished by guards, so they might be considered trivially distinguishable at the event level without needing an evaluated guard.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: NL-CONTRACT-NL4-GUARDDISJOINT-1 requires the two DoorOpenWithItem closing alternatives (to DoorShutWithItem when zero cooking time is set, or to ReadytoCook when cooking time is entered) to be distinguished by mutually exclusive evaluated conditions on the closing trigger so exactly one target is reached deterministically.
